name: Bill Jones
role: Medora cowboy; elected Billings County constable in 1886
bio: Bill Jones was a Medora cowboy whom the stockmen recommended as assistant round-up foreman in April 1884; that spring he tracked down Charlie Jolly's strayed horses. In the fall of 1884 he arrested a man for setting fire to the prairie near Scoria cut and took him to jail at Mandan, an arrest the paper revisited in 1885. The Cow Boy also reported his reckless rides across the railroad bridge and a bucking bronco at the 1885 fall round-up, and in February 1886 it condemned his shooting of a dog owned by Miss Helen Wade, for which a Stark County warrant was out. In November 1886 he was elected one of Billings County's constables.
